answer: Registration is a self-assessed license. An agent names a price for its slot, pays a small tax on that figure each epoch, and any rival may buy it at that price. A farm minting a thousand fakes cannot call them worthless, since a near-zero price exposes each to instant takeover, so it pays rent proportional to headcount, forever, with no refund. Honest operators need only a few costly slots, so the bill grows with the crowd while its influence does not. The registry stays an oasis of priced names inside an ocean of anonymous traffic, a haven where nobody can rent an audience.
